disagreements: Empirical SNR: mine 6.9 (4.5 h box; 6.8-7.9 across box widths) vs pipeline 8.75. My random-phase box noise at 4.5 h is 116 ppm vs the pipeline's 91 ppm; my 1-d running-median detrend leaves ~25% more red noise. Direction is conservative, but the signal is 7 sigma, not 9, in my hands.

Period offset: mine 10.790158 d vs pipeline 10.791014 d (delta -0.00086 d). Below the BLS peak width (~0.0018 d = P*T14/baseline) and predicted transit times differ by only 1.6 h (start), 0.3 h (mid), 0.9 h (end), so the same events are counted; noted, not a real disagreement.

Depth is box-width dependent because the event is trapezoidal (T23/T14 = 0.41): my box depth is 915 ppm at 3.65 h, 801 ppm at 4.5 h (matches pipeline 796), 649 ppm at T14 = 5.9 h; trapezoid fit 891 ppm. Any quoted depth must state its box width.

Per-event depths are over-dispersed relative to white-noise errors: chi2/dof = 3.0 over 92 events (2.6 without epoch -61); pipeline reports 2.05. Five events exceed |z|>3 with white errors; the clipped weighted mean is 543 +- 72 ppm (white) vs unclipped 679 ppm. Red noise inflates per-event scatter by ~1.7x in sigma.

The strongest single event (epoch -61, BKJD 185.54, 5036 +- 733 ppm, 9 points) is a systematic: it sits 1.8 d after the Q2 safe-mode gap (no q=0 data 181.51-183.72) on a 1-2% thermal-recovery ramp. Removing it changes the T14-box depth from 649 to 598 ppm; single-event dominance 0.07, so the detection does not rest on it, but this epoch should be excluded from any evidence pack.

Per-year depths: Y4 (Q13-Q17) = 254 +- 199 ppm is 2.0 sigma below the Y1-Y3 mean (694, 842, 710 ppm); chi2 = 5.4 for 3 dof (p ~ 0.15). Not fatal, but the pipeline's quartile 2 vs 3 (1351 vs 453 ppm) also shows ~2-3 sigma over-dispersion.

Dilution test is not a host test: SAP/PSF depth ratio 0.46 equals the PSF/SAP flux ratio 0.45, i.e. the same ~1.3 e/s absolute deficit appears in both apertures (ratio 1.02 +- 0.22). The 6-px SAP aperture holds 2.2x the target's flux, dominated by the Kp 13.6 star KIC 11285496 ~9 arcsec away, on which 1.3 e/s would be only ~30 ppm. The pipeline's pixel.json (read only after my numbers) is inconclusive (median peak SNR 2.5, deficit closer to target than any other source in 3/8 quarters), so the host star remains unlocalised.

## Independent re-derivation of the kic-011285493 first-screen signal (2026-10-17)

All numbers below trace to `/home/user/ZyushgPlanet/runs/poolA_main/adversarial/kic-011285493/rederive/results.json` (SHA-256 `8d29bab1...0788`), produced by `rederive_kic011285493.py` and `supplement_depth_vs_box.py` in the same directory. No code under `pipeline/` was imported or read; `vet.json` and `pixel.json` were opened only after my results existed. Statistic names: "BLS SDE" = (power - running median over 2001 grid points) / 1.4826*MAD on my own 1-50 d likelihood periodogram; "empirical SNR" = box depth / robust std of 1500-3000 random-phase boxes on the masked re-detrended PSF flux.

### 1. Data and detrending
LIGHTCURVE_STITCHED, SAP_QUALITY == 0, FLUX (PSF) normalised by per-quarter median: 43,401 cadences, baseline 1459.5 d. Detrend: time-based 1.0 d running median, segment-aware (gaps > 0.5 d), 5-MAD clip (43,375 kept); second pass with +-1 duration masked around the transits. Robust 30-min scatter 2196 ppm.

### 2. Blind BLS 1-50 d (own geometric grid, 285,480 periods, durations 1.2-8 h)
Top peak **P = 10.79001 d, BLS SDE 19.3** (raw mean/std SDE 13.6), depth 768 ppm, duration 3.96 h. Peaks 2 and 3 are the 1/2x (5.3957 d, SDE 15.4) and 1/3x (3.5965 d, SDE 13.1) aliases. **The pipeline period is recovered blind as the top peak.** Inverted-flux null (2 - f), identical search: top SDE 11.0 at 46.18 d; the real signal stands 8 SDE units above the null.

### 3. Ephemeris and transit statistics (PSF flux)
- Refined: P = 10.790158 d, t0 = 843.73888 BKJD = BJD 2455676.73888 (mid-baseline epoch), BLS-optimal box 3.65 h.
- Trapezoid fit: depth 891 ppm, T14 = 5.91 h, T23 = 2.41 h (T23/T14 = 0.41).
- Box depth vs width (random-phase empirical errors): 923 +- 138 (2.4 h), 914 +- 115 (3.65 h), **801 +- 116 ppm at 4.5 h (SNR 6.9)**, 649 +- 96 at T14 = 5.9 h (SNR 6.8). Formal white-noise error at T14 is 73 ppm, so red noise inflates the error by 1.6x.
- Odd 593 +- 127 vs even 702 +- 127 ppm: **0.6 sigma**.
- Secondary at phase 0.5: 109 ppm, 1.2 sigma; deepest off-transit box anywhere 247 ppm (2.75 sigma, phase 0.455), as expected from look-elsewhere over ~70 phases.
- Per-year depths (T14 box): 694 +- 162, 842 +- 173, 710 +- 192, **254 +- 199 ppm**; chi2 = 5.4 / 3 dof. Y4 is 2.0 sigma low.
- Transits: 98 epochs with any data, **90 with >= 50% coverage** (136 expected in the baseline). Per-event depths: 67% positive, chi2/dof = 3.0 vs constant (white errors). The strongest event (epoch -61, BKJD 185.54, 5036 +- 733 ppm) lies 1.8 d after the Q2 safe-mode gap on a 1-2% thermal-recovery ramp and is a detrending residual, not a transit; without it the T14-box depth is 598 ppm and the single-event dominance is 0.07.

### 4. SAP_FLUX vs PSF FLUX (dilution)
SAP depth 369 +- 60 ppm at 4.5 h (302 +- 48 at T14) vs PSF 801 +- 116: **ratio 0.46**, equal to the PSF/SAP median-flux ratio 0.45 (1584 vs 3519 e/s). In absolute units both apertures lose the same ~1.3 e/s (ratio 1.02 +- 0.22). The signal is therefore present in plain aperture photometry and is not a PSF-fit artefact, but the SAP aperture carries 2.2x the target's flux (the Kp 13.6 star KIC 11285496 ~9 arcsec away dominates it), so this test cannot identify the host: 1.3 e/s is ~30 ppm on that neighbour. Host localisation must come from the pixel-level work, which (reading pixel.json afterwards) is inconclusive: median peak SNR 2.5, deficit closer to the target than any other source in only 3 of 8 quarters.

### 5. Comparison with the pipeline (vet.json)
| quantity | mine | pipeline | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| period | 10.790158 d | 10.791014 d | agree (delta 0.00086 d < peak width 0.0018 d; events coincide to < 1.6 h) |
| depth, 4.5 h box | 801 +- 116 ppm | 796 +- 92 ppm | agree |
| duration | T14 5.9 h, T23 2.4 h, BLS box 3.65 h | 4.5 h box, TLS 3.3 h | definitional; consistent |
| empirical SNR | 6.9 (6.8-7.9) | 8.75 | mild disagreement, mine lower |
| odd/even | 0.6 sigma | 1.35 sigma | both null |
| secondary | 109 ppm, 1.2 sigma | 160 ppm, 1.76 sigma | both null |
| transits | 90 (>= 50%), 98 any | 96 events, 95 TLS distinct | agree |
| per-event scatter | chi2/dof 3.0 | 2.05 | both over-dispersed |

**Bottom line:** the 10.79 d, ~800 ppm (4.5 h box) periodic dip is real in the data and is recovered blind with my own code at BLS SDE 19 and empirical SNR ~7. Odd/even and secondary tests are null. Weaknesses to carry forward: the SNR is 7 not 9 under a more conservative noise estimate; per-event depths scatter 1.7x more than white noise; the deepest single event is a safe-mode recovery artefact; Y4 is 2 sigma shallow; and the SAP/PSF test, while confirming the dip is not a PSF-fit artefact, says nothing about which star hosts it, with the Kp 13.6 neighbour unexcluded. This remains a first-screen/stage-2 signal; it is not a candidate until the pixel-level localisation is conclusive.
sap_vs_psf_depth: SAP_FLUX depth 369 +- 60 ppm vs PSF FLUX depth 801 +- 116 ppm at a 4.5 h box (302 +- 48 vs 649 +- 96 at the 5.9 h T14 box): ratio 0.46, equal to the PSF/SAP median-flux ratio 0.45 (1584 vs 3519 e/s). Both apertures lose the same ~1.3 e/s in absolute terms (ratio 1.02 +- 0.22). Implication: the SAP aperture is diluted by a factor ~2.2 (the 6-px aperture is dominated by the Kp 13.6 neighbour KIC 11285496 ~9 arcsec away), the PSF depth is the undiluted one to quote, and the dip survives in simple aperture photometry so it is not a PSF-fitting artefact. The test does not localise the host: a 1.3 e/s deficit would be ~30 ppm on the bright neighbour, which this comparison cannot exclude.
